You can barely stand. The wound is poisoning you.
Feverish. The infection is in the blood.
You can barely stay on your feet.
You feel like you are dying.
Set, and the character knows it
Only chest compressions and a defibrillator can bring you back.
clean bed - a skin graft would close it
A blister on the burn has burst.
Something is wrong. Your veins are burning.
The wound has closed over the bullet.
dead tissue - %s of %s pieces cut away
Bring them right up to a door.
The car has to be standing still.
Needs a bottle with clean water.
Cut round each piece of dead skin to lift it off
Their heart is beating - a shock won't help.
a shaved scrape - it heals by itself
Requires a scalpel or a sharp knife
Draw the blade along the marked line, from one point to the other
Grip the bullet and pull it straight out
Grip the bullet and draw it out along the line
Still breathing. Someone beside you can bring you round.
Left alone, you will come to for a few minutes - stop the bleeding then.
You come to - stop the bleeding!
The skin graft did not take.
From the top of the strip, one even pass of the blade down it
Lay the skin over the burn - click where it goes
The graft is on, but nothing holds it down - it will take less well
Not there - it goes over the burn
No clean skin left on the thighs or upper arms to take
No stapler and staples, nor needle and thread: the graft will lie loose and take less well.
Staple it down - click each mark round its edge
Sew it down - click each mark round its edge
No stapler: the graft will be sewn down with needle and thread, which holds it less well.
A dull ache in your lower back.
The limb below the burn has died.
Their heart has stopped. Each shock costs a charge, and each one after the first is less likely to work.
Their heart has stopped. Compressions buy time and rarely restart it; a defibrillator is the real way back.
Only once nothing is bleeding. Gets them on their feet for about an hour; it does not put any blood back.
They come along the ground behind you. No running, and it wears you out fast; raising a weapon, stairs and cars make you let go.
Not examined - look at it first
The bullet is too deep in the tissue - pack the wound and take antibiotics.
You don't stitch a gunshot wound - flush it and pack it.
Needs burn cream or a herbal salve.
Hold and rub it over the burn - gently over blisters
Click on the burn to put a dab there
Your body is not clearing things the way it should.
A bitter taste, no appetite, and your hands look yellow.
The wound has closed - the packing comes away.
Queasy, and food is doing you no good.
Something you took is not agreeing with you.
Cold sweat. Your hands will not keep still.
Poisoning you. Drink water to flush it out.
That minigame is switched off in the sandbox settings.
Needs a needle and thread, or a suture needle.
Too far gone to practise on.
Nothing left on this body worth sewing.
Read the patient again without asking a second time
They are still bleeding - stop it first.
The heart is still stopped. Keep going.
The limb below the burn has gone numb and cold.
numb and cold below - cut the eschar now
The eschar is open - the blood is coming back.
it goes all the way round
The burnt limb is swelling tight.
the limb is swelling - cut the eschar
The burn has healed into a tight scar.
Too early: the wound has not closed yet and will open again.
Stretched not long ago - again in about %s h
Stitch %s of %s - press on the mark and drag across
Stitch %s of %s - no training to guide you, sew along the edge
Pull it through to the far mark
Pull it through to the other side
Requires a bandage or ripped sheets
Too much - another dose will poison you.
too long - the limb is dying
Needs a belt (not worn), a rope or a strip of cloth.
The limb below the tourniquet has gone numb.
Someone else already has hold of them.
You let go to take up your weapon.
Cut along the edge of the dead tissue
Pick the cut strips out with the tip of the blade
No tweezers - the edge will not hold still.
The blade slips off the edge.
Snip along the edge of the dead tissue

How much cover it takes to beat an infection. 1.0 is 48 hours - three antibiotics back to back, the balance the mod was built around.
Lower it on a world where medicine is scarce: 0.66 makes it a two-pill course, 0.33 a single one. Higher makes a cure a project.
It does not change how fast the illness climbs - that is the sepsis speed setting.
Chest and head fractures need rest

Ribs, a skull, a pelvis - the fractures a splint cannot reach. On: sitting down mends them measurably faster, running on them hurts, sets the bone back and drains you; painkillers dull it. Off: they heal on vanilla's flat timer, untouched by anything you do.

On: two things to do for a bleeding wound before the bandage. Press on it with your hand - a quarter of the blood loss while you hold it, hands busy. Tie a tourniquet high on an arm or leg with a belt, rope or strip of cloth - everything below stops bleeding, but past two hours the limb goes numb and past four the tissue starts dying.
Off: neither option.
Heavy bleeding leaves the survivor weak for days after the cut is dressed.

Multiplies how fast a bleeding body loses blood. 1.0 is the mod's own rate - one untreated deep wound brings on the drain on health in about three and a half hours. 2.0 is twice as fast, 0.5 half.
The stages stay where they are: going under, the drain on health and the end come at the same share of blood gone.

Multiplies how fast lost blood comes back. 1.0 is the mod's own rate - about a day to rebuild a third of the body's blood when well fed. 2.0 is twice as fast, 0.5 half.
Food and the healing traits still count on top.

A heavier survivor has more blood to lose: about 4.2 litres at 70 kg and under, 5 at 80, 5.8 at 90 and over. The same wound empties a light body faster, and the same bag of blood does less for a heavy one. Off: everybody has 5 litres, as before.

How many in-game hours drawn blood stays usable while warm. Real blood banks allow 4; the default is 8 so a trip home is possible.
A powered fridge stops the clock, a cooler slows it six times, winter air at 6 C or below keeps blood that is not being carried on a body.
A freezer ruins whole blood.

On: a burn is 1st to 4th degree. 1st heals in a day and cannot get infected, 2nd blisters and needs a dressing, 3rd and 4th have dead tissue that barely heals and feeds infection until it is cut away. Burning longer burns deeper; an uncooled fresh burn may deepen within half an hour - cool it with water. Deep burns make you thirsty.
Off: vanilla's single kind of burn.

On: right-click a fresh body (three days at most) to practise on it - stitching, trimming wound edges, and taking out a bullet if one stayed in it when it was shot. Uses the same minigames, spends what the job spends, pays three quarters of the First Aid XP of the real thing. Three sessions of sewing and trimming per body.
Each kind needs its own minigame on.

A bandaged limb shows only the bandage, a broken bone, and whether it hurts. The kind of wound, stitches and infection stay hidden until the dressing comes off.
What was examined before is remembered: removing the bandage shows it without a new examination.
Off: wounds read through the bandage as before.

On: cutting the dead tissue off a third- or fourth-degree burn opens a close-up where you run the blade round each piece yourself. Off the edge it cuts live skin.
Off: a plain timed action takes all of it off.

Writes what the mod is doing to Zomboid/Lua/Wounds_debug.log, and on a server to Wounds_debug_server.log: every condition's numbers once an in-game minute, and what each of them asked for.
For working out where health is going when nothing is visible on the panel. It does NOT enable any cheat.
Off by default: the file grows and is never cleaned up.

On: a third- or fourth-degree burn round an arm or a leg can tighten and kill the limb below unless the eschar is cut open; a debrided deep burn can be closed with skin from the thigh; a healed deep burn leaves a tight, aching scar for days. With The Only Cure a dead limb is amputated.
Off: deep burns stop at cutting the dead tissue away.

On: with a needle and an empty bag you can draw blood from another player standing next to you, not only from yourself - the donor pays the blood loss. On a server that includes a player who is unconscious and cannot refuse, so turn it on only if you trust your players.
Not yet tested in a multiplayer game.
Off: everybody draws only from their own arm.

On: cutting a tight eschar open shows the burn, and you draw the blade down it yourself.
Off: a plain timed action does it.

On: what the finding IS decides the time - a scratch is read at a glance, a laceration or a bite is real work. Two deep wounds' worth is a full examination.
Off (the default): every examination takes the flat time set by skill and the speed slider, however much or little there is to find.

How quickly an examination is carried out. Higher is faster.
First Aid still shortens it on top of this.

On: taking out a lodged bullet opens a close-up where you guide the tweezers in yourself. A shaky hand hurts and can slip.
Off: the bullet comes out the vanilla way.

A broken bone under an open wound worsens while unsplinted and feeds the infection.
Arms and legs only.
Also needs the Bone Fracture option enabled, or nothing can break in the first place.
Quick health panels wait for the examination

Only matters with Mini Health Panel or Mini Health Plus installed. Their floating window offers treatment without an examination, which walks around this mod's central rule.
On: their menu is held on an unexamined limb, same as this mod's own panel.
Off: their panel stays a fast lane - on some servers a neck wound is a matter of seconds, and one screen too many before a bandage can be a death.

On: a skin graft is three moves of your own - shaving a strip off the thigh in one even pass, laying it over the burn, then fixing it down at each mark with staples (or needle and thread).
Off: a plain timed action does it.

On: a bullet stops either in a joint - it has to come out before anything else - or deep in the tissue, where it stays: pack the wound and run antibiotics until the flesh closes over it. Gunshot wounds are packed, not stitched.
Not yet tested in a multiplayer game.
Off: bullets work exactly as in vanilla.

Turns on the blood part of the mod: drawing blood, transfusion, blood groups, typing and crossmatching - and puts the supplies for it in hospital and clinic loot: blood collection bags (single-use, the only vessel blood goes into), a transfusion set and a blood typing kit.
OFF by default. While off, none of it is offered and none of the items ever spawn - the mod stays pure Lua and can be removed at any time.
Turning it on lets mod items into your save.

Multiplies how often blood bags, transfusion sets and typing kits turn up in clinic and medical storage loot. 1.0 is the mod's own rate, 0.5 half as often, 2.0 twice - 0 removes them from loot entirely.
Only matters while the switch above is on.

A cut throat empties a survivor in well under a minute, and an untrained character spends twelve seconds looking before they are allowed to touch it.
On: the neck can be treated on sight, like vanilla.
Off: it waits for an examination like every other limb.

On: putting ointment on a burn opens a close-up where you take it out a dab at a time and rub it in yourself. Cover the whole burn, and go gently over blisters.
Off: a plain timed action that covers most of the burn.

Draws the wound close-ups - the examination panel and the stitching minigame - in a pixelated style that sits with the game's own look, instead of the drawn originals.
The wounds, the aim marks and everything they do stay exactly the same; only the rendering changes.
Off by default.

Taking more medicine than the body can clear makes you ill for far longer than the overdose itself lasts, and leaves a mark on the liver and kidneys.
Alcohol on top of a course of medicine is much harder on the liver than alcohol alone.
Water helps: a hydrated survivor clears an overdose about twice as fast, and healthy kidneys are what makes that work.
Turned off, medicine behaves as it did before this was added - an overdose still makes you sick while it lasts, but nothing accumulates.

The body always shows where it hurts and how badly. This decides how much of the naming an examination has to do first - and First Aid decides how fast and how detailed that examination is.
Everything: nothing is named until you look, treatment included.
Only what you cannot feel: an injury you watched happen is named at once, and looking is for infection, dirt and how far it has got.
Nothing: everything is named straight away, the way vanilla does it.

An untreated wound infection reaches the bloodstream and kills.
Antibiotics work as a course over days, not as a single pill.
Turned off, wound infection behaves as it does in vanilla.

How fast an infection takes hold and climbs. 1.0 is the balance the mod was built around: untreated, the first symptoms arrive after about twelve hours and it kills in roughly three days.
Lower is milder. It never makes the body recover faster, only the illness slower.

On: stitching opens a close-up of the wound and you place each stitch yourself - the needle goes in one side and out the other, and how well it is done is up to you. First Aid decides how steady your hand is; a surgical needle forgives more than a sewing one. A poor closure can tear open when you run.
Off: stitching works exactly as it does in vanilla, decided by a dice roll behind the scenes.

On the strictest examination setting, a limb cannot be treated until it has been examined - you cannot bandage what you have not looked at.
Turn this off to keep the naming behind an examination while letting first aid go ahead: you can dress a wound in a hurry and find out what it is later, somewhere safer.
Has no effect on the other two examination settings, where nothing was held back to begin with.

On: trimming a ragged wound opens a close-up where you cut the dead edge away yourself, with a scalpel or scissors. How clean the cut is decides how well the wound stitches afterwards and how much it hurts.
Off: trimming is a plain timed action, as it was before the minigame.

BETA - turn on at your own risk. Not yet tested in a multiplayer game. Reloading does not get you up - a character who was out is out again. It cannot trap anybody: after six hours down they come round whatever happened, and turning this off stands them up.

On: after losing about a third of their blood the character goes down and the screen goes dark - they cannot move or act, and they are helpless where they fell. Once the bleeding is stopped another survivor can bring them round, which buys an hour on their feet but does not put blood back; only a transfusion or time does that.
Bleed on past that and the heart can stop: then only chest compressions (which buy time) and a defibrillator (which starts it) help, and without them they die within half an hour.
Alone, they come round on their own once the bleeding has been stopped long enough. Still bleeding, they come to for a few minutes - time to put a bandage on; left open, the wound puts them under again.
Off: blood loss behaves exactly as it did before.
First Aid needed to examine while walking:

Below this First Aid level an examination roots the character in place. 0 allows walking from the start, 10 never.
Legs, feet and groin always require standing still - that is anatomy, not skill.
First Aid experience from this mod:

Multiplies the experience the mod's OWN work pays: examining a limb, trimming a laceration, drawing blood, crossmatching, running a transfusion. 1.0 is the mod's own rate, 0 pays nothing for them.
Stitching and bandaging are the game's own awards and are left alone - move those with the world's XP multiplier.
Silver sulfadiazine. Spread over a burn to keep infection out and help it heal.
Plantain or comfrey in fat. Soothes a burn and helps it heal, but keeps infection out less well than the cream.
